fichas.title: Foundation types and spread foundations
fichas.summary: Foundations may be shallow or spread—pad foundations, strip footings, ground-bearing slabs, and rafts—or deep, such as piled foundations. Masonry foundations are seldom used; unreinforced concrete is used for smaller buildings, while reinforced concrete suits higher ground pressure or wider projections. Rafts are used where subsoil bearing capacity is low or other spread foundations are insufficient. Foundations must reach frost-free depth.
uses: Provide foundations where ground-bearing capacity is low

fichas.title: Improvement of subsoil bearing capacity
fichas.summary: The page describes vibroflotation compaction, vibro stone columns, and soil stabilisation and compaction as methods to improve subsoil bearing capacity. Vibroflotation compacts soil by vibration; stone columns use aggregate without binder. Cement grouting is unsuitable for cohesive or cement-aggressive soils, while chemical grouting is limited to soils containing quartz.

fichas.title: Foundation details and load distribution
fichas.summary: Illustrations show foundation separation and expansion-joint details, raft configurations, and concrete strip-footing forms. The page warns that overlapping load areas from adjacent foundations can cause settlement or cracking. Sandfill compacted in layers can distribute loading over a wider area; other diagrams show foundations beside slopes and existing buildings.
uses: Detail foundations at separation and expansion joints
Reduce settlement and cracking risks near adjacent buildings
